metadata.title: Josh Cameron a Deep-League Option as Role Continues to Solidify
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Josh Cameron continues to see his role grow early in his rookie season. After catching two touchdowns through his first three games, Cameron hit another milestone in Week 4 with a career-high 42 receiving yards. He has now played at least 33% of the offensive snaps in three of his four games so far. That's not a very large snap share by any means, but it's still a solid mark for a rookie, and it indicates that he'd be the next man up to handle a much larger role if any of Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers, or Brian Thomas Jr. were to miss time. He's particularly appealing ahead of the upcoming trade deadline, as Thomas' name continues to come up as a trade candidate. If the Jaguars do move on from Thomas, it would be a clear sign that they believe Cameron is capable of handling increased responsibilities on offense. We've already seen him strengthen his rapport with Trevor Lawrence, and he's an intriguing option on the waiver wire, especially given the positive state of Jacksonville's offense.

metadata.title: Josh Cameron - Catches two passes vs. Cincinnati
metadata.description: Cameron hauled in both of his targets for 42 yards during the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday. He also returned two kickoffs for 45 yards.
metadata.analysis: Cameron got on the board in the second quarter with a 29-yard catch before connecting with Trevor Lawrence on a 13-yard pass in the third. The rookie sixth-rounder played 22 of the Jaguars' 61 offensive snaps (36.1 percent), fourth-most among Jacksonville's wide receivers. Cameron has a 5-74-2 receiving line on six targets through four games, and his scoring floor figures to remain limited unless the Jaguars are without one or more of Parker Washington, Brian Thomas or Jakobi Meyers. Up next for the Jaguars is a Week 5 home game against the Eagles.

metadata.title: Josh Cameron - One catch in Week 3 win
metadata.description: Cameron secured one of two targets for a 12-yard touchdown in Sunday's 35-6 win over the Patriots.
metadata.analysis: Cameron got the scoring started early in the second quarter, catching the first of Trevor Lawrence's three touchdowns. Cameron played 23 offensive snaps against New England, the same amount as Brian Thomas behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers, who both played 50 snaps on offense. Cameron could be pushing Thomas for the WR3 role in Jacksonville.

metadata.title: Josh Cameron Draws High Praise from Liam Coen
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars rookie wide receiver Josh Cameron earned high praise from head coach Liam Coen. Cameron hauled in one of two targets for 12 yards and found the end zone for the second time on just three receptions. Following the Jaguars' 35-6 dominant victory over the New England Patriots, Coen said, "Everything that he does, he does like a pro. He understands how to prepare, he's super smart, and he's selfless. And really, so many ways are what we're looking for in a Jacksonville Jaguar." Cameron ran 29% of the routes, with 44% in the slot, while former first-round pick Brian Thomas Jr. continues to see fewer snaps and opportunities. Right now, Cameron is still in a minor role in Jacksonville's crowded receiver room, but if he keeps making plays, he could be a player to monitor down the road.

metadata.title: Josh Cameron - Two returns in loss
metadata.description: Cameron returned two kicks for 50 yards in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Broncos.
metadata.analysis: Cameron played 10 offensive snaps and 14 special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver was not targeted in the contest but averaged 25 yards on his two returns.

metadata.title: Josh Cameron - Catches TD in win over Cleveland
metadata.description: Cameron caught both of his targets for 20 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: The sixth-round rookie wideout played well ahead of Travis Hunter, out-snapping him by a 19-4 margin behind the Jaguars' top trio of Parker Washington, Brian Thomas and Jakobi Meyers at wideout. Cameron ended up catching Trevor Lawrence's second touchdown, a four-yard score toward the end of the first quarter. Cameron would appear to have the lead for WR4 duties in Jacksonville.

metadata.title: Josh Cameron snags touchdown in NFL debut
metadata.description: Josh Cameron caught both of his targets for 20 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 34-10 win over the Browns on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: The rookie receiver had the wonderful experience of catching a touchdown in his first-ever regular-season game. However, it's hard to take much from it for fantasy, as the Jaguars' passing attack is incredibly spread out and Cameron is buried on the depth chart. His usage might trend up as the season goes along, and he's at least a name to monitor for dynasty formats. But don't expect anything big in the short term.

metadata.title: Josh Cameron - Two catches against Carolina
metadata.description: Cameron caught both his targets for 41 yards in Friday's 34-17 preseason loss to the Panthers.
metadata.analysis: The 2026 sixth-round pick made both his receptions in the first quarter with Nick Mullens under center, as the Jaguars rested their likely Week 1 starters on offense. Cameron is battling fellow sixth-round rookie C.J. Williams for a spot on the gameday roster, but neither should be expected to see a significant role unless injuries to Parker Washington (undisclosed) and Jakobi Meyers (hand) linger into the regular season.

metadata.title: Josh Cameron - Logs one reception in first preseason game
metadata.description: Cameron caught one of three targets for 17 yards Saturday in a 24-20 preseason win over New Orleans. He also returned one punt for 10 yards and one kick for 25 yards.
metadata.analysis: Cameron's lone catch came early in the first quarter on a connection with Nick Mullens. The rookie wideout also contributed in the return game, which may suggest that he'll have a role in that regard during the regular season. Cameron has a tough path to opportunities as a pass catcher, however, as all of Brian Thomas, Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers and Travis Hunter are firmly ahead of him on the depth chart.

metadata.title: Josh Cameron Too Far Down the Jaguars Depth Chart to Offer Value?
metadata.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars clearly viewed wide receiver Josh Cameron as one of the top remaining players on their board when they traded up to select him in the sixth round of the 2026 NFL Draft, but in a receiver room already difficult enough to sort at the top, there is no realistic potential of fantasy relevance so close to the bottom. With Brian Thomas Jr., Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers, and Travis Hunter all expected to hold their own roles in Jacksonville's offense, Cameron's clearest path to a roster spot is likely to come through special teams. Over the past three seasons at Baylor, Cameron returned 45 punts at a highly respectable 14.0-yard average, but, built more like a running back than a traditional X-receiver, his brightest future in the league could come as a kickoff returner. With some fantasy leagues adapting to the NFL's dynamic kickoff changes and rewarding return points, Cameron is not entirely unworthy of a roster spot, but in most formats, he is best left on waivers.

metadata.title: Josh Cameron has Long-Term YAC Upside in Liam Coen's Offense
metadata.description: Jacksonville Jaguars rookie sixth-round wide receiver Josh Cameron will be fighting an uphill battle for playing time in his first year in the NFL, but the 23-year-old could be a nice dynasty sleeper in rookie-only drafts later this year for his long-term upside in head coach Liam Coen's offense. Cameron put up some big numbers in his final two seasons at Baylor in 2024 and 2025, combining for 121 receptions, 1,626 yards, and 19 touchdowns. The 6-foot-2, 210-pounder has nice size, blocking skills, and yards-after-the-catch ability in a plus environment in Duval. Early on in the NFL, Cameron figures to primarily be an asset for the Jags on special teams while being buried on the WR depth chart behind Jakoi Meyers, Parker Washington, Brian Thomas Jr., and Travis Hunter. He'll also have to battle fellow rookie wideout CJ Williams. Fantasy managers in single-year fantasy leagues will want to ignore Cameron, but in rookie-only drafts, he's not a bad late-round target for long-term upside. RotoBaller currently has Cameron ranked as the No. 96 dynasty pass-catcher.

metadata.title: Josh Cameron - Added by Jacksonville
metadata.description: The Jaguars selected Cameron in the sixth round of the 2026 NFL Draft, 191st overall.
metadata.analysis: Cameron (6-foot-1, 220 pounds) played five years at Baylor and started every game in each of his final two seasons, making use of his big-bodied frame to total 19 touchdowns from 2024-25. As a rookie with Jacksonville, Cameron may successfully carve out opportunities as a situational big-play threat, but to earn a larger role than that at the NFL level he'll need to make significant developmental strides as a route runner. With Brian Thomas, Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and dual DB/WR Travis Hunter (knee) all demanding opportunities in the Jaguars' wide receiver room, there likely won't be many snaps for Cameron to compete with against Tim Jones, Austin Trammell and Chandler Brayboy.

metadata.title: Josh Cameron selected No. 191 by Jacksonville Jaguars
metadata.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars have selected WR Josh Cameron with the No. 191 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
metadata.analysis: The Jacksonville Jaguars have a plethora of wide receivers after investing first-round picks in back-to-back years on Brian Thomas Jr. and Travis Hunter. They also have Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington, leaving little to no opportunity for Josh Cameron to have a fantasy impact without significant injuries to the team's wide receiver corps.

metadata.title: Josh Cameron (calf) on track to be fully healthy for rookie minicamp
metadata.description: Baylor WR Josh Cameron is on track to be fully healthy by rookie minicamp.
metadata.analysis: Cameron suffered a calf strain at the Combine. He has spent time with 15 teams on visits, including the Falcons most recently.
